Crohn’s disease is a chronic, transmural inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any part of the gastrointestinal tract from mouth to anus. However, the terminal/distal ileum is the most commonly affected site, either alone or together with the colon (ileocolitis). The disease is characteristically segmental (“skip lesions”), with areas of affected bowel separated by relatively normal mucosa. Transmural inflammation can lead to fistulae, strictures, abscesses, and creeping fat. Rectal involvement is less characteristic than in ulcerative colitis. Therefore, among the given options, distal ileum is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common Crohn’s site → terminal/distal ileum.

  • Crohn’s → transmural inflammation.

  • Characteristic → skip lesions.

  • Complications → strictures, fistulae, abscesses.

  • Crohn’s can affect anywhere from mouth to anus.

Exam Pearl:
Crohn’s disease: think “terminal ileum + skip lesions + transmural inflammation.”

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৩) Which organism is common for meningitis in neonates?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In neonatal meningitis, the most important bacterial pathogens include Group B Streptococcus, Escherichia coli (particularly strains with K1 antigen), and Listeria monocytogenes. Among the options given, E. coli is the best answer. Neonates are particularly susceptible to these organisms because of immature immune defenses and exposure during the perinatal period. H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, and N. meningitidis are more characteristic causes of meningitis in older infants, children, adolescents, or adults depending on age and vaccination status. Therefore, E. coli is the appropriate choice from the listed options.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Neonatal meningitis → GBS, E. coli, Listeria.

  • E. coli K1 → important neonatal meningitis strain.

  • GBS → major pathogen in early-onset neonatal infection.

  • N. meningitidis → classically important in adolescents/young adults.

  • S. pneumoniae → important cause in older children/adults.

Exam Pearl:
Neonatal meningitis: remember GBS, E. coli, and Listeria.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৪) Krukenberg tumor is the metastatic gastrointestinal tumor to the......?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A Krukenberg tumor is a metastatic tumor involving the ovary, classically arising from a gastric adenocarcinoma, especially diffuse-type adenocarcinoma with signet-ring cells. The metastasis is usually bilateral and occurs through lymphatic or hematogenous spread. Although the stomach is the classic primary site, other gastrointestinal and occasionally non-GI primaries can produce Krukenberg tumors. The ovarian tumor typically contains mucin-filled signet-ring cells within the ovarian stroma. In contrast, an umbilical metastasis is classically called a Sister Mary Joseph nodule. Therefore, the correct answer is the ovaries.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Krukenberg tumor → ovarian metastasis.

  • Classic primary → stomach.

  • Histology → signet-ring cells with mucin.

  • Usually → bilateral ovarian involvement.

  • Umbilical metastasis → Sister Mary Joseph nodule.

Exam Pearl:
Krukenberg = metastatic gastric cancer to the ovaries, often bilateral and signet-ring type.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৫) Councilman bodies are found in...... Injury?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Councilman bodies are acidophilic (eosinophilic) apoptotic hepatocytes seen in the liver during certain forms of viral hepatitis, classically yellow fever and also other acute viral hepatitis. They represent hepatocyte death caused by apoptosis. Histologically, they appear as shrunken, intensely eosinophilic cells with fragmented or pyknotic nuclei. They are therefore a marker of hepatocellular injury rather than renal, intestinal, or neuronal injury. Among the given options, the liver is clearly the correct site.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Councilman bodies → apoptotic hepatocytes.

  • Site → liver.

  • Classically associated → yellow fever.

  • Also seen in → acute viral hepatitis.

  • Histology → eosinophilic, shrunken apoptotic hepatocytes.

Exam Pearl:
Councilman body = apoptotic hepatocyte in viral hepatitis, especially yellow fever.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৬) What type of hypersensitivity reaction occurs in AGN?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Acute glomerulonephritis (AGN), particularly post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, is primarily a Type III hypersensitivity reaction mediated by immune complexes. Antigen–antibody complexes become deposited in the glomeruli and activate the complement system, leading to recruitment of inflammatory cells and glomerular injury. This results in features such as hematuria, proteinuria, edema, and hypertension. In post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis, granular deposition of immunoglobulins and complement can be demonstrated along the glomerular basement membrane. Type I is IgE-mediated, Type II involves antibodies directed against fixed cellular or tissue antigens, and Type IV is T-cell mediated.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Post-streptococcal AGN → Type III hypersensitivity.

  • Mechanism → immune-complex deposition.

  • Complement activation → glomerular inflammation.

  • IF → granular (“lumpy-bumpy”) IgG/C3 deposition.

  • Type IV → T-cell mediated, delayed hypersensitivity.

Exam Pearl:
Post-streptococcal glomerulonephritis = Type III immune-complex hypersensitivity.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৭) Which is most most dangerous renal cell carcinoma?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Among the listed renal cell carcinoma (RCC) subtypes, clear cell RCC is the most common and is generally associated with the most aggressive behavior and poorer prognosis, particularly when advanced or metastatic. It accounts for the majority of RCCs and commonly arises from the proximal tubular epithelium. Clear cell RCC is characterized by lipid- and glycogen-rich cytoplasm and is strongly associated with abnormalities of the VHL gene pathway. Papillary RCC is the second most common subtype and often has a better prognosis, while chromophobe RCC generally has a relatively favorable prognosis. Urothelial carcinoma is a different renal/urinary tract malignancy rather than a subtype of RCC.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Most common RCC → Clear cell RCC.

  • Clear cell RCC → proximal tubular origin.

  • Classic molecular association → VHL inactivation.

  • Papillary RCC → second most common.

  • Chromophobe RCC → generally better prognosis.

Exam Pearl:
Clear cell RCC is the commonest and classically the most clinically aggressive RCC subtype.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৮) Adult polycystic kidney disease is a...........disorder?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Adult polycystic kidney disease, more accurately termed autosomal dominant polycystic kidney disease (ADPKD), is an autosomal dominant inherited disorder characterized by progressive development of multiple renal cysts, often accompanied by extrarenal manifestations. The most common genetic abnormalities involve PKD1 on chromosome 16 and PKD2 on chromosome 4, affecting polycystin proteins. Patients typically present in adulthood with hypertension, abdominal/flank pain, hematuria, and progressive chronic kidney disease. Important extrarenal associations include intracranial berry aneurysms, hepatic cysts, and cardiac valve abnormalities. Autosomal recessive polycystic kidney disease usually presents in infancy or childhood.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Adult polycystic kidney disease → Autosomal dominant.

  • Genes → PKD1, PKD2.

  • Major complication → chronic kidney disease.

  • Associated with → intracranial berry aneurysm and hepatic cysts.

  • Childhood polycystic kidney disease → usually autosomal recessive.

Exam Pearl:
Adult = ADPKD; childhood = ARPKD.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৭৯) Cough and sputum on most days for at least 3 months, in each of 2 consecutive years is called--?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chronic bronchitis is clinically defined as cough and sputum production on most days for at least 3 months in each of 2 consecutive years, after excluding other causes of chronic productive cough. It is a clinical definition and is commonly associated with COPD, but chronic bronchitis and COPD are not synonymous. Emphysema is defined pathologically by permanent enlargement of airspaces distal to the terminal bronchioles with destruction of their walls. COPD is a broader disease characterized by persistent airflow limitation, usually due to airway and/or alveolar abnormalities. Therefore, the specific definition given in the question is chronic bronchitis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chronic bronchitis → ≥3 months/year for ≥2 consecutive years.

  • It is a clinical diagnosis.

  • Commonly associated with → COPD.

  • Emphysema → primarily a pathological diagnosis.

  • Chronic productive cough alone does not necessarily mean COPD.

Exam Pearl:
3 months × 2 consecutive years = chronic bronchitis.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮০) Which is a feature of primary tuberculosis?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).option2: Both endogenous & exogenous source of infection
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Primary tuberculosis occurs in a person who has not previously been sensitized to Mycobacterium tuberculosis. The characteristic pulmonary lesion is the Ghon focus, typically a small area of consolidation in the subpleural region, often in the lower part of the upper lobe or upper part of the lower lobe. The Ghon focus together with involvement of regional hilar lymph nodes forms the Ghon complex. Primary TB is more common in children and may follow exogenous infection. In contrast, adult-type secondary TB commonly results from reactivation (endogenous infection) and typically affects the apical regions of the lungs. Therefore, subpleural lesion is the correct feature.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Primary TB → Ghon focus.

  • Ghon focus → typically subpleural.

  • Ghon complex → Ghon focus + hilar lymphadenopathy.

  • Primary TB → more common in children.

  • Secondary TB → classically apical/upper-lobe disease.

Exam Pearl:
Primary TB = subpleural Ghon focus + hilar lymph node involvement.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮১) Oat cell carcinoma is a variant of which lung tumor?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Oat cell carcinoma is the traditional histological term for small cell carcinoma of the lung (SCLC). It is a high-grade neuroendocrine carcinoma characterized by small cells with scant cytoplasm, finely granular chromatin, and nuclear molding. SCLC is strongly associated with cigarette smoking, usually arises centrally near the major bronchi, and has a marked tendency for early metastasis. It may also produce paraneoplastic syndromes, particularly SIADH, ectopic ACTH production, and Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome. The other options are non-small-cell lung cancer subtypes and are not called oat cell carcinoma.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Oat cell carcinoma = Small cell carcinoma.

  • Strong association → smoking.

  • Neuroendocrine tumor → high-grade, rapidly proliferating.

  • Common paraneoplastic syndromes → SIADH, ectopic ACTH, Lambert-Eaton syndrome.

  • SCLC is highly sensitive to chemotherapy and radiotherapy, but commonly relapses.

Exam Pearl:
Oat cell carcinoma = Small cell carcinoma of the lung.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮২) What type of emphysema usually occurs in cigarette smokers?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Centriacinar (centrilobular) emphysema is the type most strongly associated with cigarette smoking. It predominantly affects the respiratory bronchioles in the central portion of the acinus, while the distal alveoli are relatively preserved, especially in early disease. It has a characteristic predominance in the upper lobes. In contrast, panacinar emphysema involves the entire acinus more uniformly and is classically associated with α1-antitrypsin deficiency, often affecting the lower lobes. Paraseptal emphysema involves the distal acinus adjacent to pleura and septa and is associated with spontaneous pneumothorax, particularly in young adults. Irregular emphysema is usually associated with scarring.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Smoking → centriacinar emphysema.

  • Centriacinar → predominantly upper lobes.

  • α1-antitrypsin deficiency → panacinar, lower lobes.

  • Paraseptal → associated with spontaneous pneumothorax.

  • Centriacinar → respiratory bronchioles predominantly affected.

Exam Pearl:
Cigarette smoker = centriacinar emphysema, especially in the upper lobes.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৩) Pseudogout is related to excessive....... ?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Pseudogout is caused by deposition of calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) crystals in joints, producing acute inflammatory arthritis. It commonly affects the knee and other large joints, particularly in older adults. The crystals are typically rhomboid-shaped and weakly positively birefringent under polarized light microscopy. This differs from gout, which is caused by deposition of monosodium urate crystals that are needle-shaped and strongly negatively birefringent. The term “excessive calcium pyrophosphate” in the question refers to CPPD crystal deposition, rather than simply an elevated serum calcium level.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Pseudogout → CPPD crystal deposition.

  • Crystal shape → rhomboid.

  • Birefringence → weakly positive.

  • Common joint → knee.

  • Gout → monosodium urate, needle-shaped, negatively birefringent.

Exam Pearl:
Pseudogout = Calcium pyrophosphate dihydrate (CPPD) deposition.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৪) Loss or suppression of cough reflex during anesthesia or coma leads to which type of pneumonia?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Aspiration pneumonia occurs when gastric contents, oropharyngeal secretions, or other foreign material enter the lower respiratory tract, causing chemical injury and/or infection. Suppression or loss of the cough and gag reflex during anesthesia, coma, seizures, or impaired consciousness markedly increases the risk of aspiration because airway protective mechanisms are compromised. Aspiration commonly affects dependent portions of the lung, with the exact site depending on the patient's position. Nosocomial pneumonia is defined by healthcare-associated acquisition and is not specifically caused by loss of the cough reflex. Necrotizing pneumonia refers to severe pulmonary infection with tissue destruction.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Loss of cough/gag reflex → aspiration risk.

  • Risk factors → anesthesia, coma, seizures, impaired consciousness.

  • Common aspirate → oropharyngeal/gastric contents.

  • Dependent lung segments are commonly affected.

  • Aspiration can cause chemical pneumonitis or bacterial pneumonia.

Exam Pearl:
Suppressed airway protective reflexes + aspiration of material = aspiration pneumonia.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৫) In a patient with typhoid fever spleen becomes palpable on..?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In enteric (typhoid) fever, splenomegaly is a recognized clinical finding and usually develops during the second week of illness. The spleen may become palpable around the 7th–10th day, although the exact timing can vary depending on disease severity and prior antibiotic treatment. Splenomegaly results from systemic reticuloendothelial activation and proliferation during the infection. Other classical features include sustained or stepwise fever, relative bradycardia in some patients, abdominal symptoms, and rose spots. Among the given options, 7th–10th day is the most accepted exam answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Typhoid splenomegaly → typically second week.

  • Spleen may become palpable around 7th–10th day.

  • Rose spots → usually appear during the second week.

  • Typhoid → systemic infection caused by Salmonella Typhi.

  • Splenomegaly reflects reticuloendothelial system activation.

Exam Pearl:
Typhoid spleen becomes palpable classically around the 2nd week, often 7th–10th day.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৬) HIV virus preferentially infects & kills which portion of T lymphocyte?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
HIV preferentially infects CD4-positive T lymphocytes, particularly activated CD4⁺ helper T cells. Viral entry occurs when the HIV envelope glycoprotein gp120 binds to the CD4 receptor, followed by interaction with a chemokine co-receptor, mainly CCR5 or CXCR4. Progressive destruction and dysfunction of CD4⁺ T cells leads to cell-mediated immunodeficiency, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic infections and certain malignancies. CD8⁺ T cells are not the primary target, although their function may become impaired during advanced HIV infection. CD2 and CD6 are surface markers but are not the defining receptor for HIV entry.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • HIV primary target → CD4⁺ T lymphocytes.

  • Viral attachment → gp120 binds CD4.

  • Co-receptors → CCR5, CXCR4.

  • Progressive CD4 decline → immunodeficiency.

  • AIDS → severe cellular immune dysfunction.

Exam Pearl:
HIV targets CD4⁺ T cells: gp120 binds CD4, then CCR5/CXCR4.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৭) Which is the main site of colonization of staphylococcus aureus?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
The anterior nares (nose) are the principal site of colonization by Staphylococcus aureus in humans. Approximately a proportion of healthy individuals are persistent or intermittent nasal carriers. Nasal carriage is clinically important because colonized individuals can serve as a reservoir for transmission and may develop infections such as skin and soft-tissue infections, wound infections, or bacteremia. The organism can also colonize the skin and perineum, but the anterior nares are the classic and most important colonization site tested in examinations. Therefore, among the given options, the nose is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Main S. aureus colonization site → anterior nares.

  • Other sites → skin, axilla, perineum.

  • Nasal carriage → important reservoir for transmission and infection.

  • S. aureus → Gram-positive cocci in clusters.

  • MRSA → commonly screened using nasal swabs.

Exam Pearl:
S. aureus loves the anterior nares — nose is the classic colonization site.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৮) The definitive diagnosis of HIV can be done by which analysis method?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Traditionally, Western blot was used as a confirmatory test for HIV infection after a reactive screening test such as ELISA. ELISA is highly sensitive and commonly used for screening, while Western blot detects antibodies directed against specific HIV proteins, providing greater specificity. RIA is not the standard confirmatory test, and Southern blot is used for detecting specific DNA sequences, not routine HIV diagnosis.

Important modern note: Current HIV diagnostic algorithms generally do not use Western blot routinely; they use a laboratory HIV-1/2 antigen/antibody immunoassay followed by an HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation assay, with nucleic-acid testing when indicated. But for this traditional exam MCQ, the expected answer is Western blot.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Traditional screening → ELISA

  • Traditional confirmatory test → Western blot

  • Western blot → detects antibodies against specific HIV proteins

  • Modern confirmation → HIV-1/HIV-2 differentiation immunoassay

Exam Pearl:
Old exam rule: ELISA = screening; Western blot = confirmation.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৮৯) Which test is done to detect bilirubin in urine?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Foucher’s test is a classical chemical test used for the detection of bilirubin in urine. It is based on the oxidation of bilirubin to biliverdin, producing a characteristic green color. Urinary bilirubin is conjugated (direct) bilirubin, because unconjugated bilirubin is albumin-bound and not filtered by the kidneys. Benedict’s test detects reducing sugars, while Rothera’s test detects ketone bodies. Orthotolidine is associated with detection of occult blood.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Bilirubin in urine → Foucher’s test.

  • Benedict’s test → reducing sugars.

  • Rothera’s test → ketone bodies.

  • Orthotolidine → occult blood.

  • Urinary bilirubin → conjugated bilirubin.

Exam Pearl:
Foucher = bilirubin; Rothera = ketone bodies; Benedict = reducing sugar.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯০) Obvious internal haemorrhage are called......Haemorrhage?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A revealed hemorrhage is an internal hemorrhage in which the bleeding becomes visible externally through a natural body opening. Examples include hematemesis (vomiting blood), melena/hematochezia (blood passed through the gastrointestinal tract), hematuria (blood in urine), and hemoptysis (coughing blood). In contrast, a concealed hemorrhage occurs internally without external evidence, such as bleeding into the peritoneal or pleural cavity. Primary hemorrhage refers to bleeding occurring immediately after injury, while reactionary hemorrhage occurs after a temporary cessation of bleeding, typically within the first 24 hours.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Revealed hemorrhage → internal bleeding visible externally.

  • Concealed hemorrhage → bleeding remains inside the body.

  • Primary hemorrhage → occurs immediately after injury.

  • Reactionary hemorrhage → occurs after initial hemostasis, usually within 24 hours.

  • Secondary hemorrhage → usually due to infection/sloughing of vessels.

Exam Pearl:
Internal bleeding that becomes apparent externally = revealed hemorrhage.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯১) Which type of toxin is most important in pathogenesis of gas gangrene?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Gas gangrene (clostridial myonecrosis) is most commonly caused by Clostridium perfringens. Its most important virulence factor is the alpha toxin (lecithinase/phospholipase C). This toxin damages cell membranes by hydrolyzing phospholipids, producing extensive muscle necrosis, hemolysis, tissue destruction, and edema. It is central to the pathogenesis of gas gangrene. C. perfringens produces several toxins, but alpha toxin is the principal toxin responsible for the severe tissue damage.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Gas gangrene → commonly C. perfringens.

  • Main toxin → α-toxin.

  • α-toxin = lecithinase / phospholipase C.

  • Causes → membrane destruction, myonecrosis + hemolysis.

  • Characteristic → gas production in infected tissues.

Exam Pearl:
Gas gangrene + C. perfringens → Alpha toxin (lecithinase).

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯২) Toxoid vaccine is applicable for the prevention of.....?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A toxoid vaccine is made from a bacterial exotoxin that has been inactivated so that it loses its toxicity but retains its ability to stimulate protective antibody production. The classic example is the tetanus toxoid vaccine, which protects against the effects of tetanospasmin produced by Clostridium tetani. Toxoid vaccines are also used against diphtheria. Gas gangrene and most food poisoning/diarrheal diseases are not prevented by routine toxoid vaccination. Therefore, among the given options, tetanus is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Tetanus → toxoid vaccine.

  • Diphtheria → toxoid vaccine.

  • Toxoid → inactivated exotoxin.

  • Produces antitoxin antibodies.

  • Tetanus vaccine does not contain live C. tetani.

Exam Pearl:
Toxoid vaccines: think Tetanus + Diphtheria (Td/Tdap/DTaP).

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৩) Break bone fever is characteristic of which disease?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
“Break-bone fever” is the classic term used for dengue fever, reflecting the severe muscle, joint, and bone pain that can occur during the illness. Dengue is caused by the dengue virus, transmitted mainly by Aedes mosquitoes. Other common features include high fever, severe headache, retro-orbital pain, myalgia, arthralgia, rash, and sometimes thrombocytopenia. The term “break-bone” does not indicate actual bone fracture; it describes the characteristic intensity of musculoskeletal pain. Therefore, dengue is the correct answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Break-bone fever → Dengue.

  • Vector → Aedes mosquito.

  • Severe muscle/joint pain → characteristic.

  • Retro-orbital pain → common feature.

  • Severe dengue → may cause bleeding and shock.

Exam Pearl:
“Break-bone fever” = Dengue fever.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৪) Usually Tuberculosis doesn't occur in which of the following?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Tuberculosis can involve many organs outside the lungs, including the skin (cutaneous TB), intestine (intestinal TB), and brain/meninges (tuberculous meningitis). However, primary tuberculosis of the thyroid gland is extremely rare and is not a usual site of TB involvement. The thyroid appears relatively resistant to Mycobacterium tuberculosis because of factors such as its rich blood supply, encapsulation, and biochemical environment. Therefore, among the given options, thyroid gland is the best answer.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • TB can affect → skin, intestine, brain/meninges.

  • Thyroid TB → very rare.

  • Common extrapulmonary TB → lymph nodes, pleura, bones/joints, meninges.

  • Tuberculous meningitis → important form of CNS TB.

Exam Pearl:
TB can occur almost anywhere, but thyroid involvement is exceptionally rare.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৫) Elderly hypertensive patient presented with anemia mostly due to....?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
In an elderly hypertensive patient, anemia is commonly associated with chronic kidney disease (CKD). Long-standing hypertension can cause chronic renal damage, and reduced kidney function leads to decreased production of erythropoietin (EPO), resulting in a typically normocytic, normochromic anemia. CKD-associated anemia can also be worsened by iron deficiency, inflammation, shortened red-cell survival, and nutritional factors. In contrast, acute kidney injury (AKI) does not usually cause significant anemia unless there is bleeding or another associated cause. Acute glomerulonephritis and nephrotic syndrome are also not the typical explanation for this presentation.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • CKD → ↓ erythropoietin → anemia.

  • Typical anemia → normocytic, normochromic.

  • Long-standing hypertension → important cause of CKD.

  • AKI → usually does not cause marked anemia by itself.

  • CKD anemia → consider iron deficiency + inflammation as additional factors.

Exam Pearl:
Elderly + hypertension + anemia → think CKD with reduced erythropoietin.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৬) Chalky white area found in which type of necrosis?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Fat necrosis classically produces a chalky white, soap-like appearance due to saponification. When pancreatic lipase is released, it breaks down triglycerides into free fatty acids. These fatty acids combine with calcium to form insoluble calcium soaps, producing the characteristic chalky white deposits. This is classically seen in acute pancreatitis and can also occur after trauma to fatty tissue, such as breast fat necrosis. Caseous necrosis has a soft, cheese-like appearance and is classically associated with tuberculosis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Chalky white appearance → Fat necrosis.

  • Mechanism → saponification.

  • Fatty acids + Ca²⁺ → calcium soaps.

  • Classic setting → acute pancreatitis.

  • Caseous necrosis → cheese-like, classically TB.

Exam Pearl:
Chalky white + calcium soap = fat necrosis.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৭) Common cold is an example of which type of inflammation?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Common cold is a classic example of catarrhal inflammation, which occurs on mucous membranes and is characterized by excessive production of mucus. In common cold (acute viral rhinitis), the nasal mucosa becomes congested and edematous, with increased mucus secretion causing runny nose and nasal discharge. Catarrhal inflammation is therefore particularly associated with mucosal surfaces of the respiratory tract. Serous inflammation produces a thin, watery fluid, while fibrinous inflammation produces fibrin-rich exudate and is seen in conditions such as fibrinous pericarditis. Necrotizing inflammation involves tissue destruction.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Common cold → Catarrhal inflammation.

  • Catarrhal → mucus-rich inflammation of mucous membranes.

  • Serous → thin, watery exudate.

  • Fibrinous → fibrin-rich exudate.

  • Necrotizing → prominent tissue destruction.

Exam Pearl:
Common cold = catarrhal inflammation.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৮) Migration of leukocyte to the site of injury is termed as--?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Chemotaxis is the directed migration of leukocytes toward the site of injury in response to chemical attractants. These chemotactic substances include C5a, LTB4, IL-8, and bacterial products. Leukocytes first undergo margination and rolling, followed by adhesion to the endothelium, diapedesis (transmigration) through the vessel wall, and then chemotaxis toward the site of injury. Therefore, although diapedesis is the process by which leukocytes cross the endothelium, the directed movement toward the injury site is chemotaxis.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Leukocyte movement toward injury → Chemotaxis.

  • Crossing vascular endothelium → Diapedesis.

  • Enhanced recognition of microbes → Opsonization.

  • Engulfment and destruction → Phagocytosis.

  • Important chemotactic factors → C5a, LTB4, IL-8.

Exam Pearl:
Chemotaxis = movement toward the chemical signal; diapedesis = movement through the vessel wall.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ৯৯) Red infarct doesn’t occur in---?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
A red (hemorrhagic) infarct occurs when blood enters the infarcted area, commonly in organs with a dual blood supply, loose tissue, or venous occlusion. The lung is a classic example because it has dual blood supply from pulmonary and bronchial arteries. Small intestine and ovary can also develop hemorrhagic infarction, particularly with venous obstruction or torsion. The heart, however, has a relatively end-arterial coronary circulation, so infarction is typically pale (white/anemic) rather than red.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • Red infarct → lung, intestine, ovary, venous occlusion.

  • White infarct → heart, kidney, spleen.

  • Lung → red infarct due to dual blood supply.

  • Heart → classically white infarct.

Exam Pearl:
Heart = white infarct; lung = red infarct.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০০) Hemorrhagic shock occurs with acute loss of blood about---of total blood?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
Hemorrhagic (hypovolemic) shock typically develops when there is an acute loss of approximately 25–30% of total circulating blood volume. Among the given options, 25% is the best answer. Blood loss of around 15% may produce mild tachycardia with relatively maintained blood pressure, while around 30–40% loss causes severe shock with marked hypotension and impaired organ perfusion.

High-Yield Rapid Recall:

  • <15% → usually minimal signs.

  • 15–30% → tachycardia, anxiety, reduced pulse pressure.

  • ~25% → clinically significant hypovolemia/shock.

  • 30–40% → severe hemorrhagic shock.

  • >40% → life-threatening, profound shock.

Exam Pearl:
Acute loss of about 25% of blood volume → hemorrhagic shock.

Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).question: ১০১) 'ক্যান্সারের সঙ্গে বসবাস' বইটি কার রচনা?
Final Model Test-05 (২০০ নাম্বার).exp:
ক্যান্সারের সঙ্গে বসবাস’ বইটি বাংলাদেশের জনপ্রিয় কথাসাহিত্যিক হুমায়ূন আহমেদ রচনা করেছেন। বইটিতে তাঁর ক্যান্সারের সঙ্গে লড়াই ও ব্যক্তিগত অভিজ্ঞতার প্রতিফলন রয়েছে।

Exam Pearl:
